name: Curve pools (Vyper bug)
tldr: The pools had a reentrancy lock, but some versions of the Vyper compiler built it wrong. The lock silently did nothing.
what: Curve is one of the largest exchanges for similar assets. Several pools were written in Vyper, a Python-like smart contract language.
happened: Attackers re-entered pool functions while they were still running and drained pools used by Curve, Alchemix, JPEG'D and Metronome.
bug: In some Vyper versions, the nonreentrant guard used mismatched storage slots in different functions, so it never actually blocked reentry.
prevent: Track known compiler bugs, test the compiled contract's behavior, and treat the toolchain as part of the audit scope.
lesson: Your tools are part of the attack surface. Correct source code is not the same as correct bytecode.
